item.description: - **Changmun tells you whether its AI can run.** The last step of onboarding, and the AI panel until you first use it, now say whether Claude Code is on this Mac. If it isn't, you get a link to it, and a note that you can point Changmun at a copy it didn't find in Settings › AI. Codex, Gemini CLI and opencode are named as coming when they're what your Mac has. Until Claude Code is there, the panel's composer stays off instead of failing when you press Return. - **Fewer "Allow" questions from Claude Code.** An AI connected through MCP, such as a Claude Code session, can now be allowed on a site for the rest of its session, as the AI panel could already. It still asks again after reading another site, and anything that pays, sends, posts or deletes is still asked about every time. Commands from the command line are still asked each time.

- **Changmun updates itself.** New versions now arrive inside the app. Changmun looks for one once a day and asks before installing it; choose Changmun › Check for Updates… to look right away, or let it download and install updates on its own in Settings › Advanced. Every update is signed by the developer, and Changmun refuses one that isn't. This is the last version you need to install by hand, so the sidebar's brew note is gone. Homebrew keeps working and now knows that Changmun keeps itself up to date.
